en.title: Percy Jackson Dominates Google Searches, Outpacing Harry Potter
en.summary: New data reveals the enduring power of demigods, as the Percy Jackson series claims the top spot for most Googled book franchise. The boy wizard, once king, settles for second place in this surprising digital showdown.
en.body:
When it comes to the books captivating global imaginations online, the titans have shifted. A recent analysis of Google searches from 2025, conducted by Awesome Books, has crowned **Rick Riordan's Percy Jackson & The Olympians** series as the most searched-for book franchise. With over half a million searches, Percy's adventures in the world of Greek mythology have officially surpassed the boy wizard who once defined a generation.

For many, the surprise isn't that Percy Jackson is popular, but that it has *outranked* **J.K. Rowling's Harry Potter**. The beloved boy wizard, a consistent powerhouse in pop culture, landed in second place, commanding nearly 20% fewer searches than its demigod counterpart. This data paints a fascinating picture of current fan interest, showing that while nostalgia for Hogwarts remains strong, the call of Camp Half-Blood is resonating louder in the digital sphere.

## The Top 10 Franchises Unveiled

The full top 10 list offers a compelling snapshot of the literary landscape's most discussed series. Following Percy Jackson and Harry Potter, **J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings** secures a strong third place with 277,941 searches. The list also showcases the robust appeal of modern fantasy and YA epics, with **Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass** series at number four and **Robert Jordan's The Wheel of Time** at number five. **Suzanne Collins's The Hunger Games** rounds out the top half of the list.

What's particularly delightful is the inclusion of series that might not immediately spring to mind. **Junie B. Jones**, the mischievous elementary school student created by **Barbara Park**, makes an impressive appearance at number seven, proving that early chapter books still hold a special place in readers' hearts and search histories. **Stephenie Meyer's Twilight** saga and **R.L. Stine's Goosebumps** series also feature, demonstrating the lasting impact of their respective genres.

## Why the Digital Buzz Matters

This surge in searches for **Percy Jackson** speaks volumes about the franchise's enduring appeal and its ability to connect with new generations of readers. The upcoming Disney+ series adaptation has undoubtedly fueled renewed interest, drawing both long-time fans eager for a faithful rendition and newcomers curious about the world of demigods and monsters. It highlights how successful screen adaptations can reignite conversations and drive engagement with the source material, keeping these stories vibrant and relevant.

The data, gathered from over 80 franchises, underscores a dynamic reading community that actively engages with its favorite stories online. Whether they're looking for plot details, fan theories, or news about upcoming adaptations, readers are using search engines as a primary tool to explore their literary passions. The continued strength of these series, even years after their initial releases, is a testament to the power of compelling storytelling.

## What's Next for These Beloved Series

With the **Percy Jackson** series gaining significant momentum online, fans are eagerly anticipating further news regarding its television adaptation and any potential new literary endeavors from **Rick Riordan**. The success seen in these search trends suggests a bright future for mythological retellings and adventure stories that resonate across age groups.

I would have been wrong.
